headline: Central Government in close watch on the situation arising out of the flash flood in Nepal
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Central Government in close watch on the situation arising out of the flash flood in Nepal

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh regarding the disaster in Nepal

Devastation caused by the floods in Nepal is deeply tragic, my condolences are with the families who have lost loved ones in this disaster

Government of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis

In border areas likely to be affected, the local administration and rescue teams, along with NDRF, have been placed on high alert

26 AUG 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government in close watch on the situation arising out of the flash flood in Nepal. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh regarding the disaster in Nepal.

Union Home Minister in his post on ‘X’ said that, the devastation caused by the floods in Nepal is deeply tragic. My condolences are with the families who have lost loved ones in this disaster. The Government of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis. I spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh regarding the disaster in Nepal. In border areas likely to be affected, the local administration and rescue teams, along with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), have been placed on high alert.

As per the Advisory of the Central Water Commission (CWC) and media reports, a sudden rise in river water level in the Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal, around 160 km from the Indian border, due to suspected Flash flood/GLOF activity near the Nepal–China border, has been reported. The impact of flood is likely to travel downstream in the Gandak river, in India.

State government of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have taken measures such as required evacuation and other support to local Indian communities near the India–Nepal border. Both states have been advised to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the situation.

Officers of Ministry of Home Affairs along with Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Ministry of Defence are continuously monitoring the situation. As per CWC, the water level on Nepal side reservoirs is reducing and the situation is under control. No panic-like situation has arisen.

There are report of missing Indian tourists in Nepal territory and MEA/Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has issued emergency numbers for assistance and information regarding Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Nepal. People requiring assistance can contact the embassy on helpline +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500.

नेपाल में आई बाढ़ की विभीषिका अत्यंत दु:खद है। जिन परिवारों ने इस आपदा में अपने प्रियजनों को खोया है, मेरी संवेदनाएँ उनके साथ हैं। संकट की इस घड़ी में भारत सरकार नेपाल के साथ खड़ी है।

नेपाल में आई इस आपदा के संबंध में बिहार व उत्तर प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्रियों से बात की। इसका…

### OVERVIEW
The Central Government, led by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, is actively monitoring the flash flood situation in Nepal that has affected border areas in India. Shah spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, and rescue teams including NDRF have been placed on high alert in vulnerable border regions.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Date of Release:** 26 August 2026
- **Cause:** Sudden rise in Trishuli river water level at Furke Khola in Nepal, 160 km from the Indian border, due to suspected flash flood/GLOF activity near the Nepal-China border
- **Affected River Basin:** Impact expected to travel downstream through the Gandak river in India
- **States on Alert:** Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
- **Preparedness Measures:** Local administration and rescue teams, along with NDRF, placed on high alert in border areas
- **Response Actions:** Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have implemented evacuation measures and support for local communities near the India-Nepal border
- **Monitoring:** Officers from Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Jal Shakti, and Ministry of Defence are continuously monitoring the situation
- **Current Status:** Central Water Commission reports water levels in Nepal-side reservoirs are reducing; situation described as under control with no panic-like situation reported
- **Indian Nationals:** Reports of missing Indian tourists in Nepal territory
- **Emergency Contacts:** Indian Embassy in Kathmandu helplines: +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500

headline: India’s Sugar Industry
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

India’s Sugar Industry

Understanding the Sector, Value Chain, and Recent Price Rise

26 AUG 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi

India’s Sugar Industry at a Glance

India’s sugar industry is a major agricultural, industrial, and rural livelihood ecosystem. India is the world’s second-largest sugarcane producer. The sugarcane sector supports nearly 5 crore farmers and around 5 lakh workers in sugar factories and its allied industries.

India’s sugarcane production has reached 500 MMT in 2025-26 as per the Third Advance Estimate of Production released by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. This marks approximately 43.5 percent growth over the last 10 years, compared with 348.44 MMT of production in 2015-16.

The area under sugarcane cultivation has also increased from 49.27 lakh hectares in 2015-16 to 58.87 lakh hectares in 2025-26.

Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are the top sugarcane-producing states in India.

India exported 8 lakh MT of sugar in 2025-26, compared with 0.47 lakh MT in 2016-17.

Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane for the sugar season 2026-27 (October - September) has been set at ₹365/quintal by the government. This provides a basic recovery rate of 10.25%. This price is ₹135 more than the FRP for the sugar season 2016-17, which was fixed at ₹230/quintal with a basic recovery rate of 9.5%.

Major export destinations of Indian sugar include Sri Lanka, West Asia, and East Africa.

Adequate sugar buffer stocks are available, and sugar production in 2025–26 is expected to remain sufficient.

The Role of the Indian Sugar Industry in Advancing Ethanol Blending

The blending of ethanol with petrol is aimed at reducing dependence on fossil fuels and enhancing energy security. This move is in sync with the government's push for sustainable fuel alternatives. This initiative also supports farmers by providing them with a stable income and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, this does not mean that ethanol blending would lead to a shortage in sugar for domestic consumption.

The share of sugar diverted for ethanol production has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26.

Moreover, nearly three-fourths of the ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize.

In fact, the ethanol programme has helped sugarcane farmers and strengthened sugar mills:

On an average, India produces around 300-340 lakh MT of sugar annually.

India’s domestic sugar consumption is around 280-290 lakh MT annually.

In years of surplus production, excess stocks block the funds of sugar mills and delay payments to sugarcane farmers. Diversion of excess sugar towards ethanol has helped address this structural problem and improved the financial health of sugar mills.

As of August 20, 2026, 97% of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 sugar season have already been paid to farmers.

The improved financial position of sugar mills has reduced their dependence on government support.

Simultaneously, retail sugar prices for consumers have also remained broadly stable, increasing by only around 3% annually between August 2024 and July 2026.

Analysing the Current Sugar Price Hike

Sugar prices have increased in recent weeks, from ₹48.18 per kg on July 20, 2026, to ₹55.70 per kg on August 20, 2026. This reflects an increase of around 15.6% within one month. It's worth distinguishing this recent movement from the longer-term trend, however: as noted earlier, sugar prices rose by only about 3% annually between August 2024 and July 2026. This suggests the current uptick largely reflects short-term supply and market factors, rather than a shift in the underlying price trend.

The present increase in sugar prices is due to a combination of factors, including:

Lower-than-expected domestic production,

Increased demand ahead of the festive season,

Weather-related damage to the sugarcane crop,

Tightening global sugar supplies and rising prices, and

Speculation and hoarding by some sections of the industry.

Sugar production during the current season is expected to be around 306 LMT, compared to the initial estimate of around 343 LMT. Production has been affected by two factors: Red Rot and Top Borer disease, and waterlogging caused by excess rainfall. However, despite the lower-than-estimated production, adequate sugar stocks are available in the country to meet domestic demand. The new crushing season will begin in October.

The tightening of sugar supplies is a global phenomenon and is not limited just to India. The global sugar deficit for 2026-27 is estimated at around 33 lakh MT. As a result, international sugar prices have risen sharply from $474/tonnes on June 30, 2026 to $552/tonnes on August 20, 2026. This marks an increase of over 16% in less than two months.

Table 1: Myth v/s Fact of Rising Sugar Prices

Ethanol diversion caused the sugar price rise. | Sugar diverted to ethanol production fell from 12% in 2022–23 to around 9% in 2025–26.

Ethanol is taking away sugar from consumers. | Nearly three-fourths of India’s ethanol now comes from grains, particularly maize.

India is facing a sugar shortage. | Adequate stocks are available to meet domestic demand until the new crushing season begins.

Global sugar prices have remained stable. | International prices rose from $474 to $552 per tonne, increasing over 16% in less than two months.

India’s sugar production has collapsed. | Current production is estimated at 306 LMT, below the initial estimate of 343 LMT.

Sugar prices have been continuously rising sharply. | Long-term prices increased by only around 3% annually between August 2024 and July 2026. Current hike price is short-term.

The government has observed that speculation and hoarding by some sugar mills and traders have also contributed to the recent price increase.

Government Efforts to Curb Hoarding of Sugar and Increase Supply

The government has taken the following steps to control the short-term price hike in sugar and curb the ongoing sugar hoarding:

A stock limit of 400 tonnes has been imposed on sugar dealers across the country from August 1, 2026, to November 30, 2026.

From September 1, 2026, onwards, bulk consumers will not be permitted to hold sugar stocks exceeding 15 days of consumption.

Joint teams of central and state government officials are conducting physical verification of sugar stocks at mills to check for hoarding and artificial scarcity.

As a precautionary measure, the government has decided to permit duty-free import of 10 lakh MT of raw sugar to augment domestic availability.

States and sugar mills have been advised to begin crushing from October 15, 2026. This is expected to raise October sugar production from the usual 3-4 lakh MT to more than 10 lakh MT. This would improve availability during the festive season.

Looking Beyond the Current Price Rise

India’s sugar sector has evolved into a diversified industry that supports farmers, mills, energy production, and global trade. Recent price pressures reflect lower production, seasonal demand, global supply conditions, and market practices. However, these pressures remain temporary against the sector’s broader growth and diversification. The government’s priority remains balancing consumer interests, timely farmer payments, and industry stability.

### OVERVIEW
India's sugar industry reported a significant production increase to 500 MMT in 2025-26, representing approximately 43.5 percent growth over the past decade, while the government set the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for the 2026-27 sugar season at ₹365 per quintal with a basic recovery rate of 10.25%.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Production Growth**: Sugarcane production reached 500 MMT in 2025-26, up from 348.44 MMT in 2015-16; area under cultivation increased from 49.27 lakh hectares to 58.87 lakh hectares.
- **Top States**: Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are the leading sugarcane-producing states.
- **Exports**: India exported 8 lakh MT of sugar in 2025-26, compared to 0.47 lakh MT in 2016-17.
- **Price Setting**: The FRP for 2026-27 was set at ₹365/quintal (a decrease from ₹230/quintal in 2016-17), reflecting a basic recovery rate of 10.25%.
- **Ethanol Diversion**: Share of sugar diverted for ethanol production declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to approximately 9% in 2025-26; nearly three-fourths of ethanol now originates from grains, particularly maize.
- **Domestic Consumption**: Annual domestic sugar consumption stands at 280-290 lakh MT.
- **Payment Status**: As of August 20, 2026, 97% of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 season had been paid to farmers.
- **Retail Prices**: Consumer retail sugar prices have remained broadly stable, rising by approximately 3% annually between August 2024 and July 2026.
- **Recent Price Increase**: Sugar prices rose from ₹48.18 per kg on July 20, 2026, to ₹55.70 per kg on August 20, 2026—a 15.6% monthly increase—driven by lower production, increased demand, weather-related crop damage, tightening global supplies, and speculation/hoarding.
- **Production Forecast**: Current season production is estimated at 306 LMT, below the initial estimate of 343 LMT, impacted by red rot, top borer disease, and waterlogging.
- **Global Context**: The global sugar deficit for 2026-27 is estimated at 33 lakh MT, with international prices rising from $474/tonne on June 30, 2026, to $552/tonne on August 20, 2026 (an increase of over 16%).
- **Government Measures**: Stock limits of 400 tonnes were imposed on sugar dealers from August 1 to November 30, 2026; bulk consumers were restricted to holding sugar stocks for no more than 15 days starting September 1, 2026; joint government teams began physical verification of sugar stocks at mills; and duty-free imports of 10 lakh MT of raw sugar were permitted as a precautionary measure.
